title: They made it beautiful! #broadway #musicaltheatre #sondheim
transcript: The most epic thing I ever did as an annoying theatre kid was make the sacred pilgrimage to the actual location where my favorite musical takes place. And it turned out to be very different from what the musical led me to believe, but in a good way. Now going to the real life location of your favorite musical would have been very easy for me if my favorite musical was Dogfight or A Flower Drum Song which take place in my hometown. But as it turns out my favorite musical is Sunday in the park with George which takes place on Ile de la Grande Jatte in Paris. I went with my friend Mark in 2014 shortly after we had been in the musical together where I played George and he played Louis. And boy did we milk this for all it was worth. We took photos of everything we possibly could that even had the slightest reference to some deep cut line of dialogue in Sunday in the park with George. “Stands there staring up at the lamps” “They were talking about you at La Coupole” “Louise, don't throw stones at the ducks,” “the dog!” and so, so much more. Incidentally, this is a photo of my first legal drink because I was in Europe at eighteen. But by far the most annoying thing we did was sit in the middle of a field and sing the entirety of the song Sunday. There is video evidence of this, but you have Not earned it. But what I found most moving about this experience is that the park was so much nicer than Act 2 of the musical led us to believe. You might remember that, pivotally, in Act 2 of Sunday, George “returns” to La Grande Jatte to find it soulless and overbuilt. I don't know if they did some work on it in the intervening decades, but the park was lovely. So it was kind of like I was in my very own third act of the musical. A teenager who played George on stage makes his own trip to the island to find that the soul of the park has returned. Or maybe never left.
